glossary.definition: In AI, a hallucination is when a model confidently states something false, a fake statistic, a made-up citation, or an invented fact, because it's generating plausible-sounding text rather than actually retrieving something it verified. It's less like lying, which implies knowing the truth and hiding it, and more like a very confident student improvising a convincing-sounding answer on an exam question they never actually studied. It remains one of the central unsolved problems in trusting LLMs for anything high-stakes.

items.title: The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
items.summary: The PC gaming mods repository Nexus Mods is making disclosures about AI mandatory for uploads of new mods, meaning that mod authors will have to declare "whether AI has been used in their work," the site announced today as part of a big post about AI-generated content on the platform. items.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device from scratch in under a week
items.summary: OpenAI's hardware team used GPT-6 Astra to design a device for the Codex coding agent in under a week, handling everything from the enclosure to the circuit board to the firmware. Several revision rounds were needed before production because the model didn't always account for manufacturing tolerances. A newer internal model scores significantly higher on OpenAI's engineering benchmark, though the company isn't sharing details. OpenAI's hardware team reportedly used GPT-6 Astra to design a device that lets users talk to the Codex coding agent, finishing it as a side project in under a week.

items.title: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
items.summary: The New York Times and other newspaper companies sued Brave Software yesterday, alleging that the browser maker illegally bypasses paywalls and sells stolen news content to AI companies. "Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere," the NYT alleged in a lawsuit filed in US District Court for the Southern District of New York. items.title: Apple’s Q4 results show the enterprise tide turning to local AI
items.summary: While delivering  record Q4 revenue , Apple’s financial results revealed a  $33 billion cost  associated with memory price inflation, representing the true cost of the  growing bubble of AI data center investments . The results also showed something that threatens those same data center investments — a sea change in how enterprises are approaching AI. Inference costs, security, and  data governance concerns  may finally be dampening enthusiasm for cloud-based AI services. Apple revealed several major enterprise clients who are turning to its products as  solutions for local inference .

items.title: Here’s Why You Shouldn’t Use AI to Vote
items.summary: From hallucinations to partisan bias, artificial intelligence chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude are not helpful when it comes to Election Day. As Americans go to the polls today, many will have had their decision about who to vote for informed by an artificial intelligence –powered chatbot. Around 50 percen t of recently surveyed US adults have at one time used an AI chatbot, and 8 percent say they have used these tools ahead of the midterms to find information on candidates and policies, according to Pew Research. But a lot of information from these chatbots is out of date and has been hallucinated or sourced from partisan websites.

items.title: Snowflake launches Business Ontology to boost AI agent reliability
items.summary: Snowflake is hoping to improve the reliability of AI agents with a new tool called Business Ontology, as part of its Horizon Catalog, meant for data discovery, management, and governance. Horizon Catalog received a boost in June with the launch of Horizon Context , a set of semantic and metadata management capabilities to help enterprises collect, enrich, and organize metadata across their data estates and give AI agents a better understanding of enterprise data, its relationships, and how it is used. Business Ontology builds on that foundation by allowing enterprises to define and approve business concepts, assign owners to those definitions, and link them directly to the underlying tables and views, Snowflake said in a statement. That, in turn, should give enterprise AI agents access to authoritative business definitions, such as what constitutes net revenue, rather than relying on competing interpretations of the same data across different systems, it added.

items.title: Coforge Is Outgrowing Its Larger Rivals. Is AI the Reason?
items.summary: Coforge’s growth is beginning to outpace that of its larger rivals. But the headline numbers tell only part of the story. The IT services company is expanding through acquisitions, deepening relationships with existing clients and betting that artificial intelligence (AI) can help it grow without adding costs at the same pace. The distinction matters. Coforge reported revenue of ₹6,170 crores for Q2 FY27, up 53.6% year on year (40.1% in dollar terms).

items.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
items.summary: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law, hack into unauthorized servers, or release poison gas into major cities and kill us all. Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear. Claude, for instance, has its constitution —a sort of moral code.

items.title: India floats AI plan under which ‘The model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model’
items.summary: As debate and legal argument continue over the extent to which developers of large language models are entitled to feed the world’s data into their systems without paying for it, India’s government has come up with an idea to regulate and secure the flow of information. India’s motive is to create AI models trained on local data, because it thinks offshore model-makers won’t be motivated to address the nation’s issues or to ensure owners of data stay in control. ” The scheme envisions “Training Data Providers” (TDPs) – examples of which include hospitals, banks, and government agencies – sharing anonymized and encrypted data with a “Data Exchange Platform” (DEP). Entities called “Training Data Consumers” (TDCs) access the data stored at the DEPs to train their models.
